text:
marc: Heads-up — proposal to reduce cross-service chatter by merging request-enricher + session-stitcher into a single 'enrichment-core' boundary. I sketched a phased plan, want quick feedback. TL;DR: consolidation for latency/ops savings, keep runtime toggle & gradual traffic migration. :thinking:

anya: Curious — what's the expected QPS delta and peak memory implications? Are we talking extra headroom per pod?

marc: Good q. Ballpark: 10-15% lower p99 latency for enrichment-heavy flows; mem +15-25% per pod under worst-case state. We save network hops and serialization CPU. I'll paste a microbenchmark later.

sam: Caveat: stateful KV ownership will change. We'll need an upgrade path for the existing KV namespace and migration script. Also routing layer needs to be able to shadow traffic to the new service.

tessa: From test standpoint: we should have a compatibility suite (schema + behavior) and a canary harness that can replay historical traces. I can own the replay harness if we agree.

marc: Agree. Migration approach I'm thinking: 1) implement enrichment-core behind feature-flag 2) dual-write for reads until warm 3) traffic shadowing + golden canary 4) flip reads after confidence. Add circuit-breaker fallback to old services.

anya: Sounds sensible. For feature flags — propose this format:
```
feature: enrichment_core
env: prod
rollout: pct(0->10->50->100)
fallback: session-stitcher
metrics: latency,enrichment_failures
```

sam: I'll build the shadowing hook in the router and a per-tenant opt-out. Also need an ops runbook for rollback if caching mismatches surface.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: enchant-proto branch -> staging at 2026-07-12T09:00Z

tessa: Timeline: prototype in 2 weeks, integration test week 3, staging canary week 4. Owner: anya (proto), sam (router), tessa (tests). I'll add Jira tickets.

marc: Decision: proceed with prototype. Keep coupling surface minimal (public API unchanged). Weekly sync Wed 11am. Action items: anya(owned), sam(owned), tessa(owned). I'll post the microbenchmarks and a short design doc in #architecture later today. :thumbsup:
